Where it began

Matt Renshaw was born in Middlesbrough, England, in 1996. At seven he moved with his family to New Zealand, and at ten to Australia, so by the time he reached Brisbane Grammar School he had already seen a fair bit of the cricketing world.

He made his first first-class hundred for Queensland in December 2015, against New South Wales in the Sheffield Shield, and within a year he was in the Test side.

The player

His first Test came in November 2016 against South Africa, as an opener in place of his Queensland partner Joe Burns, with Ian Healy handing him his baggy green. In only his fourth match, at Sydney, he made 184 against Pakistan. He was the first Australian to reach 500 Test runs before his 21st birthday.

The years after that brought recalls in 2018 and 2023, and plenty of runs elsewhere, before a Test to treasure in 2026. In Durban, coming in at 3 for 84, he made 190, at the time his highest Test score, sharing a stand of 134 for the ninth wicket with Nathan Lyon. He added 82 in the second innings, took his first Test wicket, finished with 2 for 30 and was named Player of the Match as Australia won by 214 runs. By November 2026 he had played 18 Tests and made 1,022 runs at 35.24, with two hundreds and five fifties.

What made him special

Adaptability and appetite. He has opened, batted in the middle order and bowled a little, and on his ODI debut against India at Perth in October 2025 he made 21 not out and hit the winning run. Later, in Harare, came a first one-day hundred, 109 from 94 balls.

The Test side did not always find room for him, and there were spells of years in between. He simply went away and scored runs, which is the most persuasive argument a batter can make.

Away from the middle

He has spent several seasons in English county cricket. On his first appearance for Somerset, in April 2018, he made 101 not out, precisely half of the side's 202, and he came back for further spells in 2022 and 2024, with a stint at Kent in between. At home he has played Big Bash cricket for the Brisbane Heat and the Adelaide Strikers. He was named in the Sheffield Shield team of the year in March 2018 after making 686 runs.

And finally

In December 2018, turning out for Toombul in Brisbane club cricket, he made 345, then a record for the city's senior game. It took him 273 balls and included 12 sixes. The bowlers that day are entitled to tell the story however they like.
